en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn to turn English sentences around for emphasis, the way speakers, writers and storytellers do. Let's start!

steps.title: Turning a sentence around
steps.text: Quick recap: *If I had known, I would have come* (third conditional). Today: a more formal, more dramatic way to say things, called **inversion**.
steps.body:
**Inversion** = the **auxiliary** (helping verb: *have, has, had, do, does, did, is, was, will, should*) moves **in front of the subject**, like in a question.
Normal: *I have **never** worked with such a great team.*
Inverted: ***Never have I** worked with such a great team.*
But it's **not a question**: it ends with a full stop, and your voice goes down.
It happens when a **negative word** opens the sentence: *never, rarely, seldom, not only, under no circumstances…*

pairs.id: kata kerja bantu (have, do, will, should…)

steps.title: The Indonesian trap
steps.text: Indonesian can put *belum pernah* or *jarang* first too, but the rest stays the same: *Belum pernah **saya melihat**…* English also swaps the subject and the auxiliary.
steps.body: Wrong (Indonesian order): *Never I have seen such a mess.* Right: ***Never have I** seen such a mess.* Only the auxiliary moves; the main verb stays after the subject.

examples.en: Seldom has the city faced such heavy floods.
examples.id: Jarang sekali kota ini menghadapi banjir separah ini.

examples.en: Never have we had so many volunteers.
examples.id: Belum pernah kami punya relawan sebanyak ini.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
examples.id: Dalam keadaan apa pun, jangan bagikan kata sandimu.

examples.en: Not only has Sari finished the report, but she has also checked the figures.
examples.id: Sari tidak hanya sudah menyelesaikan laporannya, tetapi juga sudah memeriksa angka-angkanya.

steps.title: A press conference
steps.text: Pak Hasan from the Ministry of Education is opening a press conference about a new scholarship programme. He wants to sound strong.

options: Rarely the ministry has received so many applications.
Rarely has the ministry received so many applications.
Rarely has received the ministry so many applications.
question.explanation: After a negative word at the start, the **auxiliary** *has* goes **before the subject** *the ministry*, and the main verb *received* stays after it. The first sentence keeps the Indonesian order; the third moves the main verb too.

steps.title: No helping verb? Add do
steps.text: What if the normal sentence has **no auxiliary**, like *We rarely meet*? Then you borrow **do / does / did**, just like in a question.
steps.body:
*We rarely meet.* → ***Rarely do we meet.*** (not *Rarely we meet*, not *Rarely meet we*)
*She speaks French.* → ***Not only does she speak** French, but she also speaks Spanish.*
*I had no idea.* → ***Little did I know** that…*
After *do / does / did* the verb goes back to its **base form**: *does she **speak***, not *speaks*.
With **be**, nothing to add: ***Rarely is** the office this quiet.*

pairs.id: he / she / it: tambah does, -s hilang

pairs.en: the office is → is the office

steps.title: Welcoming the interns
steps.text: Bu Ani, the head of HR, is giving a speech to welcome this year's interns. She wants to praise their first project.

question.prompt: Arrange the words, starting with Rarely: Jarang sekali kami melihat hasil sebagus ini.
question.solution: Rarely do we see such good results.
question.explanation: *Rarely* opens the sentence, and *We see* has no auxiliary, so add **do** before the subject: *do we see*. The verb stays in the base form: *see*.

steps.title: Openers with a partner
steps.text: Some openers come with a partner word, or put the inversion in the **second** part of the sentence.
steps.body: *Hardly … **when***, *No sooner … **than*** (don't swap them). After *Only after / Only when + time*, invert the **second** part. **No inversion** when the negative word belongs to the subject: *Only Budi knew*, *Hardly anyone came*.

examples.en: Hardly had I sat down when my manager called me.
examples.id: Baru saja saya duduk, atasan saya sudah menelepon.

examples.en: No sooner had the train left than it started to rain.
examples.id: Begitu keretanya berangkat, langsung turun hujan.

examples.en: Only after the audit did we see the real problem.
examples.id: Baru setelah audit kami melihat masalah yang sebenarnya.

examples.en: Little did Rina know that her boss was listening.
examples.id: Rina sama sekali tidak tahu bahwa atasannya sedang mendengarkan.

examples.en: Only Budi knew the password.
examples.id: Hanya Budi yang tahu kata sandinya. (tanpa inversi: only Budi = subjek)

steps.title: If without if
steps.text: Remember *If I had known…* from the third conditional? In formal English you can drop **if** and start with the auxiliary.
steps.body:
Only three words do this:
- ***Had** I known*, … = If I had known (imagined past)
- ***Should** you need* help, … = If you need help (may happen; polite)
- ***Were** I to accept*, … / ***Were it not for** her*, … = If I were to accept / If it weren't for her (imagined)
No *if* with them: *If had I known* ✗.
Negative: **not** after the subject: *Had I **not** known* (not *Hadn't I known*).
*Were* for every person: *Were she…*, not *Was she…*

pairs.en: Were I to accept the offer, …
Were it not for your help, …
Had it not been for the rain, …
pairs.id: Kalau saja waktu itu tidak hujan, …

steps.title: A missed flight
steps.text: You read this in an incident report: *Had Budi checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.*

options: Budi had checked the schedule, so he didn't miss the flight to Makassar.
If Budi checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.
If Budi had checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.
question.explanation: *Had Budi checked* = **If Budi had checked**: the third conditional with *had* in front and no *if*. It's imagined: Budi **didn't** check, and he **did** miss the flight. *If Budi checked* would be about now.

steps.title: Powerful or strange?
steps.text: Inversion is never required: the normal word order is **always correct**. Inversion is a style choice: it adds emphasis, drama or formality.
steps.body:
**Sounds natural:** speeches, formal letters and emails, reports, news, telling a story for effect (*Little did I know…*).
**Sounds strange:** a quick WhatsApp, chatting with friends or family, ordering food. There it sounds dramatic, stiff or like a joke.
*Should you have any questions, please contact us* fits a company email (= *Apabila ada pertanyaan…*). To a friend, just write *If you have questions, tell me!*

steps.title: Which setting?
steps.text: Look at this sentence: *Never before has our university welcomed so many international students.*

question.prompt: Where does this sentence sound most natural?
options: In a WhatsApp to a classmate about lunch
In the rector's welcome speech at the start of the academic year
In a quick chat with your ojek driver
question.explanation: Inversion adds drama and formality, so it suits a **speech**. In a WhatsApp or a chat with the ojek driver it would sound stiff or like a joke: there you'd use the normal order (*We've never had so many…*).

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for your next speech, report or formal email!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Inversion for emphasis
artifact.intro: Inversion = the auxiliary goes before the subject, like in a question, but the sentence is a statement. Use it after a negative opener or instead of if, in formal and dramatic English.
rows: Never have I + third form
Never have I seen such a crowd.
I have never seen such a crowd.
Rarely / Seldom do we + base verb
Rarely do we meet in person.
We rarely meet in person.
Not only does she …, but she also …
Not only does she speak French, but she also speaks Spanish.
She speaks French and Spanish.
Hardly had I … when …
Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
I had only just sat down when the phone rang.
No sooner had I … than …
No sooner had we arrived than it rained.
As soon as we arrived, it rained.
Under no circumstances should …
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
You must never open this door.
Only after / when … did I …
Only when I got home did I notice it.
I only noticed it when I got home.
Little did I know …
Little did I know that he was the CEO.
I had no idea that he was the CEO.
Had I (not) known, …
Had I known, I would have called you.
If I had (not) known, …
Should you need …, …
Should you need help, please call us.
If you need help, …
Were I to …, …
Were I to move, I would choose Bandung.
If I were to move / If I moved, …
Were it not for / Had it not been for …
Were it not for my family, I would give up.
If it weren't / hadn't been for …
tips: No auxiliary in the normal sentence? Add do / does / did and use the base verb: Rarely do we meet.
Inverted conditionals: no if, not after the subject (Had I not known), were for every person.
The normal order is always correct. Invert in speeches and formal writing, not in WhatsApp chats.

examples.en: Never before has our city hosted so many guests.
examples.id: Belum pernah kota kita menerima tamu sebanyak ini.

examples.en: Should the meeting be cancelled, we will inform you by email.
examples.id: Apabila rapatnya dibatalkan, kami akan memberi tahu Anda lewat email.

examples.en: Had Rina left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the opening.
examples.id: Seandainya Rina berangkat lebih awal, dia tidak akan ketinggalan pembukaannya.

steps.text: Two clear British Council pages with extra practice: one on negative openers, one on conditionals without if.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu belajar membalik susunan kalimat bahasa Inggris untuk memberi penekanan, seperti yang dilakukan pembicara, penulis, dan pencerita. Yuk, mulai!

steps.title: Membalik susunan kalimat
steps.text: Ulasan singkat: *If I had known, I would have come* (third conditional). Hari ini: cara yang lebih formal dan lebih dramatis untuk mengatakan sesuatu, namanya **inversi**.
steps.body:
**Inversi** = **kata kerja bantu** (*have, has, had, do, does, did, is, was, will, should*) pindah **ke depan subjek**, seperti di pertanyaan.
Biasa: *I have **never** worked with such a great team.*
Inversi: ***Never have I** worked with such a great team.*
Tapi ini **bukan pertanyaan**: diakhiri titik, dan suaramu turun.
Inversi muncul kalau **kata negatif** membuka kalimat: *never, rarely, seldom, not only, under no circumstances…*

pairs.id: kata kerja bantu (have, do, will, should…)

steps.title: Jebakan bahasa Indonesia
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia juga bisa menaruh *belum pernah* atau *jarang* di depan, tapi sisanya tetap sama: *Belum pernah **saya melihat**…* Bahasa Inggris juga menukar subjek dan kata kerja bantunya.
steps.body: Salah (urutan bahasa Indonesia): *Never I have seen such a mess.* Benar: ***Never have I** seen such a mess.* Hanya kata kerja bantu yang pindah; kata kerja utama tetap setelah subjek.

examples.en: Seldom has the city faced such heavy floods.
examples.id: Jarang sekali kota ini menghadapi banjir separah ini.

examples.en: Never have we had so many volunteers.
examples.id: Belum pernah kami punya relawan sebanyak ini.

examples.en: Under no circumstances should you share your password.
examples.id: Dalam keadaan apa pun, jangan bagikan kata sandimu.

examples.en: Not only has Sari finished the report, but she has also checked the figures.
examples.id: Sari tidak hanya sudah menyelesaikan laporannya, tetapi juga sudah memeriksa angka-angkanya.

steps.title: Konferensi pers
steps.text: Pak Hasan dari Kementerian Pendidikan membuka konferensi pers tentang program beasiswa baru. Dia ingin terdengar tegas dan berkesan.

options: Rarely the ministry has received so many applications.
Rarely has the ministry received so many applications.
Rarely has received the ministry so many applications.
question.explanation: Setelah kata negatif di awal kalimat, **kata kerja bantu** *has* pindah **ke depan subjek** *the ministry*, dan kata kerja utama *received* tetap di belakangnya. Kalimat pertama memakai urutan bahasa Indonesia; kalimat ketiga ikut memindahkan kata kerja utama.

steps.title: Tidak ada kata kerja bantu? Tambah do
steps.text: Bagaimana kalau kalimat biasanya **tidak punya kata kerja bantu**, seperti *We rarely meet*? Kamu 'meminjam' **do / does / did**, persis seperti di pertanyaan.
steps.body:
*We rarely meet.* → ***Rarely do we meet.*** (bukan *Rarely we meet*, bukan *Rarely meet we*)
*She speaks French.* → ***Not only does she speak** French, but she also speaks Spanish.*
*I had no idea.* → ***Little did I know** that…*
Setelah *do / does / did*, kata kerjanya kembali ke **bentuk dasar**: *does she **speak***, bukan *speaks*.
Dengan **be**, tidak perlu tambahan: ***Rarely is** the office this quiet.*

pairs.id: he / she / it: tambah does, -s hilang

pairs.en: the office is → is the office

steps.title: Menyambut peserta magang
steps.text: Bu Ani, kepala HR, memberi sambutan untuk peserta magang tahun ini. Dia ingin memuji proyek pertama mereka.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya, dimulai dengan Rarely: Jarang sekali kami melihat hasil sebagus ini.
question.solution: Rarely do we see such good results.
question.explanation: *Rarely* membuka kalimat, dan *We see* tidak punya kata kerja bantu, jadi tambahkan **do** sebelum subjek: *do we see*. Kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: *see*.

steps.title: Pembuka dengan pasangan
steps.text: Ada pembuka yang punya pasangan kata, atau yang inversinya ada di bagian **kedua** kalimat.
steps.body: *Hardly … **when***, *No sooner … **than*** (jangan tertukar). Setelah *Only after / Only when + waktu*, yang dibalik bagian **kedua**. **Tanpa inversi** kalau kata negatifnya bagian dari subjek: *Only Budi knew*, *Hardly anyone came*.

examples.en: Hardly had I sat down when my manager called me.
examples.id: Baru saja saya duduk, atasan saya sudah menelepon.

examples.en: No sooner had the train left than it started to rain.
examples.id: Begitu keretanya berangkat, langsung turun hujan.

examples.en: Only after the audit did we see the real problem.
examples.id: Baru setelah audit kami melihat masalah yang sebenarnya.

examples.en: Little did Rina know that her boss was listening.
examples.id: Rina sama sekali tidak tahu bahwa atasannya sedang mendengarkan.

examples.en: Only Budi knew the password.
examples.id: Hanya Budi yang tahu kata sandinya. (tanpa inversi: only Budi = subjek)

steps.title: If tanpa if
steps.text: Ingat *If I had known…* dari third conditional? Dalam bahasa Inggris formal, kamu bisa membuang **if** dan memulai dengan kata kerja bantu.
steps.body:
Hanya tiga kata yang bisa:
- ***Had** I known*, … = If I had known (masa lalu khayalan)
- ***Should** you need* help, … = If you need help (mungkin terjadi; sopan)
- ***Were** I to accept*, … / ***Were it not for** her*, … = If I were to accept / If it weren't for her (khayalan)
Tanpa *if*: *If had I known* ✗.
Negatif: **not** setelah subjek: *Had I **not** known* (bukan *Hadn't I known*).
*Were* untuk semua orang: *Were she…*, bukan *Was she…*

pairs.en: Were I to accept the offer, …
Were it not for your help, …
Had it not been for the rain, …
pairs.id: Kalau saja waktu itu tidak hujan, …

steps.title: Ketinggalan pesawat
steps.text: Kamu membaca ini di laporan kejadian: *Had Budi checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.*

options: Budi had checked the schedule, so he didn't miss the flight to Makassar.
If Budi checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.
If Budi had checked the schedule, he wouldn't have missed the flight to Makassar.
question.explanation: *Had Budi checked* = **If Budi had checked**: third conditional dengan *had* di depan dan tanpa *if*. Ini khayalan: Budi **tidak** memeriksa jadwal, dan dia **memang** ketinggalan pesawat. *If Budi checked* berarti tentang sekarang.

steps.title: Berkesan atau aneh?
steps.text: Inversi tidak pernah wajib: susunan kata biasa **selalu benar**. Inversi adalah pilihan gaya: menambah penekanan, kesan dramatis, atau formal.
steps.body:
**Terdengar alami:** pidato, surat dan email resmi, laporan, berita, bercerita supaya berkesan (*Little did I know…*).
**Terdengar aneh:** WhatsApp singkat, ngobrol dengan teman atau keluarga, pesan makanan. Di situ terdengar dramatis, kaku, atau seperti bercanda.
*Should you have any questions, please contact us* cocok untuk email perusahaan (= *Apabila ada pertanyaan…*). Ke teman, cukup tulis *If you have questions, tell me!*

steps.title: Situasi yang mana?
steps.text: Perhatikan kalimat ini: *Never before has our university welcomed so many international students.*

question.prompt: Di mana kalimat ini terdengar paling alami?
options: In a WhatsApp to a classmate about lunch
In the rector's welcome speech at the start of the academic year
In a quick chat with your ojek driver
question.explanation: Inversi menambah kesan dramatis dan formal, jadi cocok untuk **pidato**. Di WhatsApp atau saat ngobrol dengan sopir ojek, kalimat ini terdengar kaku atau seperti bercanda: di situ pakai urutan biasa (*We've never had so many…*).

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk pidato, laporan, atau email resmimu berikutnya!

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Inversi untuk penekanan
artifact.intro: Inversi = kata kerja bantu diletakkan sebelum subjek, seperti di pertanyaan, tapi kalimatnya pernyataan. Pakai setelah pembuka negatif atau sebagai pengganti if, dalam bahasa Inggris yang formal dan dramatis.
rows: Never have I + bentuk ketiga
Never have I seen such a crowd.
I have never seen such a crowd.
Rarely / Seldom do we + bentuk dasar
Rarely do we meet in person.
We rarely meet in person.
Not only does she …, but she also …
Not only does she speak French, but she also speaks Spanish.
She speaks French and Spanish.
Hardly had I … when …
Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.
Baru saja saya duduk, telepon berdering.
No sooner had I … than …
No sooner had we arrived than it rained.
Begitu kami tiba, langsung hujan.
Under no circumstances should …
Under no circumstances should you open this door.
You must never open this door.
Only after / when … did I …
Only when I got home did I notice it.
I only noticed it when I got home.
Little did I know …
Little did I know that he was the CEO.
I had no idea that he was the CEO.
Had I (not) known, …
Had I known, I would have called you.
If I had (not) known, …
Should you need …, …
Should you need help, please call us.
If you need help, …
Were I to …, …
Were I to move, I would choose Bandung.
If I were to move / If I moved, …
Were it not for / Had it not been for …
Were it not for my family, I would give up.
If it weren't / hadn't been for …
tips: Tidak ada kata kerja bantu di kalimat biasa? Tambahkan do / does / did dan pakai bentuk dasar: Rarely do we meet.
Conditional dengan inversi: tanpa if, not setelah subjek (Had I not known), were untuk semua orang.
Urutan biasa selalu benar. Pakai inversi di pidato dan tulisan formal, bukan di chat WhatsApp.
